name: Bear

app.note: The bear keeps the size of the studio bear of main: the shoulder joints at 1.0 m (ANIMALS of tools/studio-body.ts). The skull top of the mesh is at 0.955 u, so at 1.5221 m for each unit it is at 1.454 m, 2% below the studio bear (1.483 m). The reach is the reach of the arm factor below at that scale.

armFactorNote: The arms keep the length of the mesh (user rule: keep the limbs of a mesh of the user, and fit the props). The conductor holds no instrument.
legFactorNote: The legs keep the length of the mesh. The bear stands on its podium, so no seat asks for longer legs.
jointsNote: The places are in the units and the axes of the studio in the pose of the source: 1 unit from the soles to the tips of the ears, the soles at y = 0, +z forward, +x the left side. The right side mirrors the left side. The probes are in docs/research/2026-10-23-bear-tpose/. The bear stands upright on short thick legs, apart below the crotch at y 0.18, with the middle of each leg cut at x 0.13. The thigh joint lies at the crotch, the ankle at the narrowest leg cut (y 0.07), the knee halfway between them, and the toes at the ball of the foot (toe tips at z 0.10). The trunk joints lie about 0.015 behind the middle of the body cut. The head starts at y 0.77, and the skull top is at 0.955. The arms are in a T-pose: each arm goes out and a little down, free of the trunk beyond x 0.18 from y 0.58 to 0.75 (sections-x.txt). The cuts across the arm axis give its middle line (arm-axis.txt). The shoulder joint lies inside the root of the arm, the elbow at x 0.31, past the end of the long faces under the upper arm, the wrist where the paw starts (x 0.40), and the forearm twist halfway between the elbow and the wrist. The finger joint lies at the root of the claws, and its tail at the tip of the claws. The ear joint lies at the root of the round ear. The short tail is a ball at y 0.25 behind the back. Each roll is the hint of the z axis of the bone, forward by default. In the T-pose, the palm faces down and forward. Of the palms and the elbows of the scan (gate-variants.txt), this pair gives the least paw twist and stretch in the arm gate: with the elbow halfway to the wrist (x 0.29), three long faces under the upper arm crossed the elbow and stretched 0.51 (limit 0.35), and with the palm straight down, the paws twisted 113 and 105 degrees.

studio.note: The bear stands on its podium in the app, so the seated bind keeps the legs of the source: each turn is the identity. The trunk does not recline (open 0). The bind arms are the values of the other meshes of the user.

armFree.note: The arm is free of the trunk beyond x 0.18 and above y 0.575, and the belly bulges out to x 0.239 below y 0.54 (sections-x.txt). A vertex of the free arm lies beyond the plane |x| = armSplit, within radius of the chain of the arm joints, and above the floor, so that the belly is not a part of it.

sliver.note: The values of the other meshes of the user.

line.note: The angle of the elephant, the rhino, and the rabbit: a lower angle mixes the weights of long arm faces.

haunch.note: The part of the thigh weight that goes to the hips grows from 0 at the knee to 1 at the thigh joint, so that the round haunch stays on the hips.

weights.note: Beyond the plane of armSplit (armFree), only the free arm follows the arm bones. Above headFrom, each vertex follows the head only. Each round ear follows its ear bone above earBase. The short tail is a ball on one bone (tailBall). clavicleFrom, armTop, and shoulderHead are the rules of the bear mesh of 2026-10-22, moved with the shoulder joint. The rig has no cut, no ring, and no split: the arms of the T-pose are free of the trunk, and the faces of the user stay (user, 2026-10-23).

tone.note: The tone of the bear mesh of 2026-10-22: the brown fur takes the darker brown of orchestra-latest.png.

colors.note: The values of samples, palette, eyeShare, and dark are the values of the bear mesh of 2026-10-22.

chair.note: The chair of the rig sets the seat top of the seated bind. The bear stands in the app, so no player sits on this seat.
